name: Zierickzee
typical_route: Vlissingen - Cape of Good Hope - Sainte-Marie - Ambon and home
note: Flagship o' the Ambon run since the first Zierickzee o' 1624; the present hull be the seventh o' the name, launched off the Schelde hard in 1978, an' still the fastest o' the four in a followin' sea.

name: Ter Veere
typical_route: Vlissingen - Baltimore - Port Royal and home
note: The Caribbean valuables ship. Her strongroom be a cask-lined hold under the great cabin with three locks an' three keyholders: the Cap'n, the Quartermaster an' the client's agent.

name: Middelburgh
typical_route: Vlissingen - Cape of Good Hope - Sainte-Marie - Ambon and home
note: Named for the town that condemns our prizes, which the hands find funny. The heaviest o' the retourschepen an' the only one carryin' a surgeon's mate as well as a surgeon.

name: De Honte
typical_route: Ambon - Banda - Ternate - Sainte-Marie, and the Pacific islands in season
note: Enrolled at Ambon an' keeps to the eastern seas. Named for the old mouth o' the Schelde by the type rule, though her sailmakers call her Si Honte; rebuilt at Ambon with teak below the waterline.

name: De Stormvoghel
typical_route: North Sea and Channel escort; Vlissingen - Baltimore
note: The Council's own jacht, an' the Captain-General's when he sails. Escorts the retourschepen out past Ushant an' comes home with the west-country letters.

name: The Gannet
typical_route: Atlantic approaches; Baltimore - Vlissingen; escort of homebound retourschepen
note: Watches the approaches from Roaringwater Bay to the Scillies. Her lookouts be paid a stuiver a sightin' an' have the best eyes in the Gilde.

name: The Frigate Bird
typical_route: Caribbean cruising ground; Port Royal - Curacao - the Havana approaches
note: Fast, long-winged an' never home empty. The Letters of Marque Division's first choice for stoppin' a mark an' readin' her papers.

name: The Pelican
typical_route: Port Royal - Cartagena - Vlissingen fast cargo (cochineal, indigo)
note: Oldest jacht on the register an' the slowest, but she carries the dyestuffs that pay the Caribbean chamber's rent. Her company voted twice to keep her rather than take a new hull.

name: Le Paille-en-queue
typical_route: Indian Ocean; Sainte-Marie - Mozambique Channel - Mauritius - the Cape
note: Named for the tropicbird with the long white tail. Guards the waterin' place an' runs the Mozambique Channel for the Division under the client's commissie.

name: Elang Laut
typical_route: Ambon - the Pacific islands (sandalwood, pearl shell); Banda Sea escort
note: The sea eagle. Built at Vlissingen to Ambon's order an' sailed out by her own sailmakers; carries the Gilde's letters to the Pacific islands an' comes back with sandalwood.

name: Gheduld
typical_route: Vlissingen - the Baltic (timber, hemp, tar) and back
note: Patience. Fetches the oak, hemp an' Stockholm tar the yard lives on; 18 hands an' a cat, an' she has never once been late for the Kermis closin'.

name: Voorsichticheyt
typical_route: Vlissingen - Norway (timber) - Vlissingen
note: Prudence. Her skipper reefs afore the squall shows an' has lost no spar in twenty years; the yard's apprentices learn the ropes aboard her.

name: Trouwe
typical_route: Vlissingen - Port Royal bulk (logwood, cacao, salt); calls at Baltimore
note: Fidelity. The Atlantic fluyt, deep an' slow; carries logwood an' salt home an' biscuit an' cordage out, an' feeds the Baltimore store on the way.

name: Rechtvaerdicheyt
typical_route: Baltimore - Skibbereen - Vlissingen (salt beef, biscuit, casks)
note: Justice. The victuallin' fluyt; every barrel o' beef in the Gilde has been aboard her, an' the hands hold the name be a joke on the cook.

name: Eendraght
typical_route: Port Royal - the cays - the Jamaican coast; warehouse tender and prize-goods carrier
note: Concord. Oldest hull on the register. Lays the prize goods along the wharf at auction an' carries sealed cargo from the sloops to the warehouse without breakin' bulk.

name: Matigheyt
typical_route: Sainte-Marie - the Madagascar mainland (rice, zebu, limes) - Mauritius
note: Temperance. Carries rice an' beef to the waterin' place from the mainland an' rum away from it, which the hands find fittin' for the name.

name: Neersticheyt
typical_route: Ambon - Banda - Ternate spice run; feeder to the retourschepen
note: Diligence. The clove fluyt; loads at Banda an' Ternate an' tranships to the retourschip at Ambon, as the first o' the name did from 1631.

name: Spaersaemheyt
typical_route: Ambon - Sainte-Marie (spices west; canvas and iron east)
note: Thrift. The canvas ship; carries sailcloth to the loft eastbound an' cloves an' nutmeg west to the retourschip at Sainte-Marie. Her boekhouder counts nails.

name: The Sou'wester
typical_route: Atlantic approaches, Roaringwater Bay to the Channel mouth, under commissie
note: Named for the wind that brings the marks in. Boards in the Channel mouth under a registered commissie an' brings 'em to Baltimore under seal for the Prize Council.

name: Squall
typical_route: Caribbean cruising ground; the Windward Passage and the Jamaica Channel
note: The Division's Caribbean workhorse. Her boardin' party drills with blunted cutlasses an' has never lost a hand, nor taken a life, in a boardin'.

name: Norther
typical_route: Caribbean cruising ground; the Yucatan Channel and the Gulf approaches
note: The cold north wind o' the Gulf. Longest sweeps an' lightest draught o' the five, built for the Yucatan shoals where the marks hide.

name: La Rafale
typical_route: Mozambique Channel and the approaches to Sainte-Marie, under commissie
note: The gust. Works the Mozambique Channel for the Division an' reads papers in French, Portuguese an' Arabic; touches no pilgrim ship, by the articles.

name: Angin Ribut
typical_route: Banda Sea and the Molucca passages, under commissie
note: The storm wind. Guards the spice run through the Molucca passages an' serves the Division's eastern commissions; her boardin' party be Ambonese an' Zeeuws in equal parts.

name: De Bode
typical_route: Vlissingen - Middelburg - Baltimore; the Kermis-year totals run
note: The messenger. Carries the chambers' totals up the Schelde to Middelburg at the Kermis closin' an' the Council's letters down. Newest hull on the register.

name: An Teachtaire
typical_route: Baltimore - the Irish and Cornish coasts - the Channel; coastal supply and dispatches
note: The messenger, in Irish. Runs water, biscuit an' letters along the coast an' meets the homebound retourschepen off the Scillies with the mails.
